claims.text: No subject-matter string of any program (e.g. 'Indus', 'sign', 'decipherment') appears in the redesigned shell — brand block, tool home, settings furniture, or tray strings — in the Spec 081 wireframes; subject content appears only as data inside a program's space.
falsification_tests: Any shell surface in the renders naming a program's subject matter — e.g. a subtitle like the current 'Indus Script Analysis', a nav label, or a tray string specific to one program.

evidence.description: Wireframes 01, 13, 15, 16 (shell surfaces) read against the specimen program's vocabulary; wireframe 17 shows a second program (Gulf Seals Survey) in the identical shell.

claims.text: Every wireframe screen has exactly one primary-styled action, and its annotation names it.
falsification_tests: A render containing zero or two or more primary-styled actions, or an annotation naming a primary action that the render does not show as primary.

evidence.description: Annotation block on each of the 17 wireframe renders; primary buttons use the single .btn.primary style.

claims.text: Every status surface in the redesign shows identity (what the thing is) and an observation time (when it was checked), never liveness alone.
falsification_tests: Any status surface in the renders that is a bare colored dot, or a state word ('Healthy', 'Running') with no identity and no observed-at time attached.

evidence.description: Service chip on all web renders ('Glossa Lab v0.1.0 · TRISTEN-DESKTOP · checked 14:02'); Status screen identity table (wireframe 14); tray tooltip and status line (wireframe 15).

claims.text: Claims are reachable from the program home in at most two clicks (home -> Claims), and the claim detail shows the falsifier plus lane 1 (machine checks) and lane 2 (human settlement) in separate, labelled regions that do not share vocabulary.
falsification_tests: A render path longer than two clicks from program home to a claim, a claim detail without a visible falsifier, or a detail where verdict words and stage words appear in one merged status.

evidence.description: Wireframe 02 (Claims in nav with count), wireframe 03 (register), wireframe 04 (detail: falsifier card, 'Lane 1 — Machine checks', 'Lane 2 — Human settlement').

claims.text: Negative verdicts (NOT SUPPORTED, FAILED jobs, INCONCLUSIVE) render with the same size, weight, and default visibility as positive ones on every surface that lists outcomes.
falsification_tests: Any render where negative outcomes are hidden behind a default-off filter, greyed, shrunk, or relegated below positive ones by default ordering.

evidence.description: Wireframe 02 latest-verdicts (two of three entries negative, unfiltered); wireframe 03 register; wireframe 08 experiment list; wireframe 09 failed job as a full-width explained row.

claims.text: A second program fits the redesigned shell without any change to shell text or structure, and creating a program requires only a name and a question (description optional).
falsification_tests: A create form requiring any subject-specific field, or a second-program render that needs shell text the first program's shell does not have.

evidence.description: Wireframe 17 (Gulf Seals Survey specimen in the identical shell); wireframe 16 create/import screen listing exactly the two required inputs; wireframe 01 program list holding both programs in the same card shape.

claims.text: Every log or history surface in the redesign states its time window, and none presents cumulative history as current state.
falsification_tests: A render showing a log stream or history list with no window stated, or cumulative counts (e.g. lifetime error totals) presented as the service's current state.

evidence.description: Wireframe 14 session log ('this session only, since 08:12', with the full file labelled a record); wireframe 15 tray door renamed to 'View status & session log'; wireframe 09 job rows carry started/finished times; wireframe 12 ledger labelled append-only history.

claims.text: Every row on the digestion board names the specific human act it is waiting for; no digestion surface shows a bare count or percentage as settlement.
falsification_tests: A digestion render whose rows lack the missing-act field, or any surface presenting a stage count/percentage as if it were understanding or settlement.

evidence.description: Wireframe 05: every card carries a 'Missing:' line naming the record owed; program home (wireframe 02) shows the queue count only with its doorway and the 'named person's recorded act' explanation.

claims.text: Wherever digestion stages render, the five stage names appear verbatim: created, checked, explained, accepted, digested.
falsification_tests: Any stage synonym in the renders (e.g. 'verified', 'approved', 'done') used as a stage name.

evidence.description: Stage tracks and chips in wireframes 03, 04, 05; teaching text in wireframe 17.

claims.text: At a 390 px mobile viewport, every screen's primary action is visible/reachable without horizontal scrolling, and the mobile bottom nav is Home / Claims / Digestion / Jobs / More.
falsification_tests: Any mobile screenshot with the primary action off-canvas or clipped, page-level horizontal scrolling, or a bottom nav elevating Discovery or AI over Claims/Digestion.

evidence.description: Mobile screenshots (wireframes/shots/*-mobile390.png) for all 17 screens; responsive rules in wireframes.css (sidebar collapses to the bottom nav, grids stack, register table scrolls inside its card only).

claims.text: Program-space navigation labels are subject-free (Home, Claims, Digestion, Evidence & sources, Data, Analysis, Experiments, Discovery, Research loop, Reports & ledger); subject-specific material appears only as content inside the program.
falsification_tests: A navigation label naming a subject concept (e.g. 'Signs', 'Decipherment') as a peer destination in program space.

evidence.description: Sidebar markup identical across wireframes 02-14 and 17, including for the Gulf Seals specimen program.

claims.text: The tray names the open program in its status line and tooltip, shows uptime in human units, and is single-instance: launching it when one is running focuses the existing tray instead of adding another.
falsification_tests: A tray render showing raw-second uptime or no program name; in phase 2, a start test that leaves two tray processes running.

evidence.description: Wireframe 15 spec sheet (status line 'Indus Script — backend healthy · v0.1.0 · up 5 h 50 m', tooltip 'Glossa Lab — Healthy (v0.1.0) · Indus Script', single-instance note answering the 2026-10-29 three-tray accumulation finding).
